title: RepositoryAnalysisResultEvent
description: Analysis worker -> backend. One event per finished analysis, success or failure. The worker never writes analysis_job or analysis_evidence: the backend owns those tables and this event is how the result reaches them.

event_id.description: Deduplication key for the consumer. Delivery is at-least-once, so the backend must treat a repeated event_id as already applied.

trace_id.description: Copied from the request event so one analysis is one trace end to end.

analysis_id.description: The backend resolves user_id and repository_id from this. The worker holds no user identity and must not carry one.

request_event_id.description: event_id of the request this answers. Lets the backend tell a genuine re-analysis apart from a redelivery of the same work.

registry_version.description: The registry the worker actually evaluated against, echoed from the request. analysis_evidence stores it, so evidence stays traceable to the rules that produced it.

commit_sha.description: The analyzed commit. Evidence permalinks are built from this plus file_path and start_line.

status.description: FAILED travels on this topic too. The DLQ is for operators; a user-visible failure has to reach the backend, or analysis_job stays QUEUED forever.

error_code.description: Required when status is FAILED, absent otherwise. Same vocabulary the worker records in repo_analysis.event_claim: REPOSITORY_NOT_FOUND, REPOSITORY_NOT_ACCESSIBLE, REPOSITORY_TOO_LARGE, CLONE_TIMEOUT, CLONE_FAILED, GIT_NOT_AVAILABLE, REGISTRY_VERSION_UNKNOWN.

error_detail.description: Operator-facing cause, typically git's stderr. Never rendered to end users; error_code is what the UI switches on.

technologies.description: Empty on failure, and legitimately empty when nothing matched.

evidence.description: Capped per rule by the worker before it gets here; maxItems is the message-size backstop, not the selection rule.

candidates.description: Dependencies that matched no registry technology. Observations only: the worker cannot know how many users a candidate affects, so the backend aggregates.

level.description: Highest rule_type satisfied for this technology. L0 found (declared dependency), L1 applied (import, config, annotation), L2 used (core API call, own contribution), L3 advanced (operational maturity).

matched_rule_ids.description: Every rule that matched, not just the one that set the level. A level with no rule behind it is not explainable, and explainability is the point of Evidence.

EvidenceItem.description: One fact that supported one rule. Maps to a row in analysis_evidence.

file_path.description: Repository-relative, forward slashes. Half of the permalink.

fact_payload.description: The matched fact's fields, keyed by the fact_field vocabulary the rules use: MODULE, COORDINATE, ECOSYSTEM, SCOPE, LANGUAGE, FILE_PATH. Stored as jsonb so a new fact type does not need a schema change here.

code_snippet.description: Optional. The checkout is deleted when the job ends, so this is the only offline copy; without it the UI needs GitHub to render the evidence.

commit_sha.description: The commit that last changed this line, from git blame. Null when authorship could not be read -- a shallow checkout, a file git could not blame, or contribution analysis turned off -- and the backend reads that as not verified rather than guessing. Deliberately the commit and not the author: deciding whose commit it is needs the requesting user's identity, and this payload travels a topic that outlives their consent.

TechnologyCandidate.description: An unmatched dependency, observed once in this analysis. Imports are deliberately not a source: an import path has no reliable package boundary in Java or C#, while a manifest entry is already the right unit.

coordinate.description: Version stripped and normalized per ecosystem: group:artifact for MAVEN, name (scope included) for NPM, PEP 503 name for PYPI, lowercased id for NUGET. Versions must not be part of it or one library fragments into a new candidate on every release.

scope.description: The declaration's scope as written (implementation, testImplementation, devDependencies, ...). Kept because a test-only dependency should not later count the same as a production one, and re-deriving it would mean re-cloning.

occurrence_count.description: Declarations within this repository, for example one per module of a multi-module build. The backend ranks by distinct users, not by this.

AnalysisStats.description: What the run saw. Operational, not user-facing: a sudden drop in files_parsed across analyses means an extractor broke, and without these numbers that looks the same as repositories getting simpler.
